---
name: all-or-none-rule-commitment-fails
description: Committing to the single smallest consistent rule (no posterior averaging) fits ~170 nats worse than the best Bayesian model
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 1 candidate 2 (2026-10-30), `smallest_rule_commitment`: commit to the smallest consistent rule out of 44 arithmetic+digit rules (span fallback), plus 2 yes-rates. Smoke-fit log-lik was about -1088, against an ELPD of -918 for `tenenbaum_digit_concepts`. Only 200 of 2250 trials needed the fallback.

**Why:** people's generalization is graded, so averaging over hypotheses (and intervals) matters. Hard MAP commitment is too coarse.
**How to apply:** don't bother with more variants of deterministic MAP/rule commitment. Graded posterior mixing is needed. See [[digit-concepts-key]].
---
name: digit-concepts-key
description: In the number-game data, "contains digit d" concepts drive much of the fit; Tenenbaum+digit rules hits ~-914 in-sample loglik with 2 params
metadata:
  type: project
---
Raw responses show digit-containment generalization (set 83,38,58,68 → yes to 84-89; 92,82,27,42 → yes to 20s), and distance-to-nearest-example barely matters. Adding 11 digit concepts (contains 0-9, ends in 0) to tenenbaum_rules_similarity (round 0, candidate_5, `tenenbaum_digit_concepts`) gave smoke-fit loglik -914.4, vs incumbent bigelow_piantadosi_independent ELPD-LOO -926.6 (45 free rule weights).

**Why:** the digit rules were the gap between Tenenbaum (-1249) and the incumbent, not the per-rule weights.
**How to apply:** future refinements should keep the digit concepts; free per-rule weights may be unnecessary.

Round 1 cand_1: `conservative_evidence_digit_concepts` (likelihood tempered by power beta, LogNormal(0,0.5)) smoke-fit loglik -913.8 — only ~0.6 better than the untempered model, so evidence tempering probably isn't where the gap is.

Round 1 (candidate_3) MAP tests on the incumbent: a free prior share for digit concepts fits omega≈0.255 (= the equal-weight 11/44, so no gain, novelty risk); freeing NOISE gives noise≈0.136, LL -910.8; a guess lapse gives lapse≈0.028, LL -909.0. Submitted the free-noise version (`digit_concepts_inferred_outlier_rate`).

name: fit-speed-budget
description: Admission fit is 7000 iters/chain warm-start NUTS; per-gradient cost must be ~<25ms; tricks that worked
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1d82c78b-0bac-4618-97c8-da7bd32baa1b
  modified: 2026-10-30T21:06:41.047Z
---

Admission fits use production draws 4000 + tune 3000 per chain (warm_start_nuts, dense mass matrix), 30-min limit per run. Machine has 1 core. Incumbent `tenenbaum_digit_concepts` logp+grad ≈ 12 ms. A memory-subset mixture over its hypothesis space (≈700 states) cost 62 ms naive → too slow (~49 min).

**Why:** the check_candidate smoke fit (200 iters) passes even when the full fit would time out.

**How to apply:** benchmark logp+dlogp time and NUTS n_steps (probe `_warm_start_sample` with small draws) before finishing. Speedups that worked: replace gathering posterior rows per cell (slow AdvancedIncSubtensor1 gradient) with a `pytensor.sparse.CSR` + `structured_dot` (44→25 ms); declaring module-level `SAMPLER_SETTINGS = {"target_accept": 0.9}` halves steps (10.8→5.3). Don't name a scratch script `timeit.py` (shadows stdlib, breaks pymc import). Related: [[digit-concepts-key]].

Also worked (2026-10-30, `order_weighted_concept_learning`): when intervals must be grouped by (size, per-position hit pattern) instead of (size, k), keep only each set's non-empty groups (≤473 of 1600 on this data) padded per set, and gather size-dependent terms by index — 47 → 18 ms.

name: hierarchical-rule-prior-shrinks
description: Partially pooled (log-normal, non-centred) rule saliences on the equal-prior lapse model shrink to tau≈0.15; ELPD ≈ incumbent
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 2 candidate_3 (2026-10-30), `hierarchical_rule_salience_with_guess_lapse`: incumbent `equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse` + log w_r = tau*z_r, tau~HalfNormal(1). Smoke loglik -905.3 (incumbent -905.8); 2x500 fit ELPD-LOO -907.9 (incumbent -908.2), p_loo 5.2, tau 0.15±0.12. Fast: 200 iters in 10 s.

**Why:** data give no support for rule-salience heterogeneity once lapse is in; free 45 weights' in-sample gain is overfitting.
**How to apply:** don't try further rule-prior variants (family weights, hierarchical, free). Novelty-gate risk: predictions ~identical to the incumbent. See [[number-game-ceiling]].
---
name: iter2-screens
description: Round 2 MAP screens on equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse (NLL 904.5): new concept families and response tweaks gain at most ~1.8 nats
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 2, candidate_4 (2026-10-30). Baseline in-sample NLL 904.5. Adding decade, repdigit, digit-sum, single-digit or "contains both digits" rules gave no gain. Logit sharpening gave 0. Free example noise gave 902.7, but lapse then drops to about 0.008, so it would duplicate `digit_concepts_inferred_outlier_rate`. A rule prior proportional to |rule|^gamma gave 903.3 with gamma≈-0.24, a slight preference for narrow rules. I submitted that as `rule_breadth_prior_concepts`. Its smoke loglik was -904.8 and the fit took about 2 s per 200 iterations.

**Why:** this confirms [[number-game-ceiling]]. Most of the residual is 5-response-per-cell binomial noise.
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these concept families. Further gains are unlikely without participant-level structure, and the CSV has no participant column.

Round 2 cand_5 repair (2026-10-30): `specificity_biased_rule_prior_lapse` was rejected as a near-duplicate of `rule_breadth_prior_concepts` (RMSE 0.0003). The repair is `occam_specificity_prior_all_concepts`, which applies the same |c|^-g to intervals too, normalised within each class and collapsed to 100 size groups per set. Smoke loglik was -904.4, about 16 s per 200 iterations. Applying g to intervals moves p_yes by RMSE ≈ 0.01 at g = 0.1, which clears the 0.002 novelty gate.

name: number-game-ceiling
description: Rule+interval+digit concept model is near its ceiling; single-param tweaks gain only 3-6 nats in-sample
metadata:
  type: project
---

Submitted `equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse` (the lapse model with one shared rule prior): smoke loglik -905.8.

**How to apply:** don't spend rounds on noise/lapse/exponent tweaks; look at the residual sets above.

name: soft-criterion-decision-rule
description: Logit criterion+gain decision rule on equal-prior digit-concept posterior gives smoke loglik -906.1, same as lapse model
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 2 candidate_2 (2026-10-30), `soft_confidence_criterion_decision`: p_yes = sigmoid(gain * (logit posterior - logit criterion)), 3 params (lambda_0, criterion, gain). Smoke loglik -906.1 vs -905.8 for `equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse`; fits in ~1 s.

**Why:** response-level mechanisms (lapse, threshold) all land around -906; confirms [[number-game-ceiling]] and [[lapse-small-gain]].
**How to apply:** decision-rule variants are saturated; don't propose more.
"""Refinement of equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse: Bayesian concept
learning over the same 45 rules and every interval of 1..100 (size principle,
10% of examples drawn uniformly), with a response lapse -- on a fraction
`lapse` of trials the participant guesses "yes" with probability `guess_yes`.
The one change: the rules' shared prior lambda_0 is not split equally but in
proportion to |rule| ** gamma, a single a-priori preference for specific
(gamma < 0) or broad (gamma > 0) rules. Each interval keeps (1 - lambda_0) / 5050.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt
from scipy.special import logsumexp

ALPHA = 0.9
NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return list(rules.values())


RULES = rule_concepts()
N_RULES = len(RULES)
INTERVALS = [list(range(m, n + 1)) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]
MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES + INTERVALS], dtype="float64")
# log P(x | h) of one example x (column x - 1) under each hypothesis.
EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * MEMBERSHIP / MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = MEMBERSHIP[:N_RULES]
LOG_RULE_SIZE = np.log(RULE_MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1))
# Centre so gamma does not trade off against lambda_0's normalisation.
LOG_RULE_SIZE_C = LOG_RULE_SIZE - LOG_RULE_SIZE.mean()

with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_log_lik = pm.Data("rule_log_lik", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))  # (sets, rules): log P(D | r)
    interval_log_evidence = pm.Data("interval_log_evidence", np.zeros(1))  # (sets,)
    interval_in_concept = pm.Data("interval_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))  # (sets, targets)
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # set index * 100 + target - 1
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    gamma = pm.Normal("gamma", 0.0, 1.0)  # prior preference for rule breadth
    log_rule_prior = gamma * LOG_RULE_SIZE_C
    log_rule_prior = log_rule_prior - pt.logsumexp(log_rule_prior)
    rule_joint = rule_log_lik + log_rule_prior[None, :]  # (sets, rules)
    rule_log_evidence = pt.logsumexp(rule_joint, axis=1)
    rule_post = pt.exp(rule_joint - rule_log_evidence[:, None])
    rule_in_concept = pt.dot(rule_post, RULE_MEMBERSHIP)  # (sets, targets)

    log_rules = pt.log(lambda_0) + rule_log_evidence
    log_intervals = pt.log1p(-lambda_0) - np.log(len(INTERVALS)) + interval_log_evidence
    p_rule = pm.math.sigmoid(log_rules - log_intervals)[:, None]
    in_concept = p_rule * rule_in_concept + (1 - p_rule) * interval_in_concept

    p_concept = pt.clip(in_concept.reshape((-1,))[row_cell], 0.0, 1.0)
    lapse = pm.Beta("lapse", 2, 8)
    guess_yes = pm.Beta("guess_yes", 2, 2)
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip((1 - lapse) * p_concept + lapse * guess_yes, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def prepare_observed(rows):
    """Rows carry `number_set` ("16,8", in presented order), `target` and `rating`."""
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    set_log_lik = np.stack([EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK[:, np.array(s) - 1].sum(axis=1) for s in unique])
    interval_log_lik = set_log_lik[:, N_RULES:]
    interval_log_evidence = logsumexp(interval_log_lik, axis=1)
    return {
        "rule_log_lik": set_log_lik[:, :N_RULES],
        "interval_log_evidence": interval_log_evidence,
        "interval_in_concept": np.exp(interval_log_lik - interval_log_evidence[:, None]) @ MEMBERSHIP[N_RULES:],
        "row_cell": np.array([index[s] * 100 + int(r["target"]) - 1 for s, r in zip(sets, rows)], dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }

"""Refinement of equal_prior_concepts_with_guess_lapse: Bayesian concept
learning over the same 45 rules and every interval of 1..100 (size principle,
10% of examples drawn uniformly), with a response lapse -- on a fraction
`lapse` of trials the participant guesses "yes" with probability `guess_yes`.
The one change: the rules' shared prior lambda_0 is not split equally but in
proportion to |rule| ** gamma, a single a-priori preference for specific
(gamma < 0) or broad (gamma > 0) rules. Each interval keeps (1 - lambda_0) / 5050.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt
from scipy.special import logsumexp

ALPHA = 0.9
NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return list(rules.values())


RULES = rule_concepts()
N_RULES = len(RULES)
INTERVALS = [list(range(m, n + 1)) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]
MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES + INTERVALS], dtype="float64")
# log P(x | h) of one example x (column x - 1) under each hypothesis.
EXAMPLE_LOG_LIK = np.log(ALPHA * MEMBERSHIP / MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True) + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = MEMBERSHIP[:N_RULES]
LOG_RULE_SIZE = np.log(RULE_MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1))
# Centre so gamma does not trade off against lambda_0's normalisation.
LOG_RULE_SIZE_C = LOG_RULE_SIZE - LOG_RULE_SIZE.mean()

with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_log_lik = pm.Data("rule_log_lik", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))  # (sets, rules): log P(D | r)
    interval_log_evidence = pm.Data("interval_log_evidence", np.zeros(1))  # (sets,)
    interval_in_concept = pm.Data("interval_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))  # (sets, targets)
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # set index * 100 + target - 1
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    gamma = pm.Normal("gamma", 0.0, 1.0)  # prior preference for rule breadth
    log_rule_prior = gamma * LOG_RULE_SIZE_C
    log_rule_prior = log_rule_prior - pt.logsumexp(log_rule_prior)
    rule_joint = rule_log_lik + log_rule_prior[None, :]  # (sets, rules)
    rule_log_evidence = pt.logsumexp(rule_joint, axis=1)
    rule_post = pt.exp(rule_joint - rule_log_evidence[:, None])
    rule_in_concept = pt.dot(rule_post, RULE_MEMBERSHIP)  # (sets, targets)

    log_rules = pt.log(lambda_0) + rule_log_evidence
    log_intervals = pt.log1p(-lambda_0) - np.log(len(INTERVALS)) + interval_log_evidence
    p_rule = pm.math.sigmoid(log_rules - log_intervals)[:, None]
    in_concept = p_rule * rule_in_concept + (1 - p_rule) * interval_in_concept

    p_concept = pt.clip(in_concept.reshape((-1,))[row_cell], 0.0, 1.0)
    lapse = pm.Beta("lapse", 2, 8)
    guess_yes = pm.Beta("guess_yes", 2, 2)
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip((1 - lapse) * p_concept + lapse * guess_yes, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))

def prepare_observed(rows):
    """Rows carry `number_set` ("16,8", in presented order), `target` and `rating`."""
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]

"""Refinement of rule_breadth_prior_concepts: Bayesian concept learning over
the same 45 rules and every interval of 1..100 (size principle, 10% of examples
drawn uniformly), with a rule prior proportional to |rule| ** gamma and a
response lapse (on a fraction `lapse` of trials the participant guesses "yes"
with probability `guess_yes`). The one change: people take it that the shown
examples are distinct, so each example is drawn from the concept's members not
yet shown (strong sampling without replacement). The likelihood of the k-th
example under concept h is 0.9 * [x in h] / (|h| - members of h already shown)
+ 0.1 / 100. This sharpens the size principle most for small, nearly
exhausted concepts.
"""

import numpy as np
import pymc as pm
import pytensor.tensor as pt
from scipy.special import logsumexp

ALPHA = 0.9
NUMBERS = np.arange(1, 101)


def rule_concepts():
    rules = {
        "odd": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 2 == 1],
        "primes": [n for n in NUMBERS if n > 1 and all(n % a for a in range(2, int(n**0.5) + 1))],
        "squares": [n * n for n in range(1, 11)],
        "cubes": [n**3 for n in range(1, 5)],
        "powers of 2, not 32": [2, 4, 8, 16, 64],
        "powers of 2, or 37": [2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 37, 64],
        "even": list(range(2, 101, 2)),
    }
    rules.update({f"multiples of {m}": list(range(m, 101, m)) for m in [3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12]})
    rules.update({f"powers of {m}": [m**k for k in range(1, 8) if m**k <= 100] for m in range(2, 11)})
    rules.update({f"ends in {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if n % 10 == d] for d in range(10)})
    rules.update({f"contains digit {d}": [n for n in NUMBERS if str(d) in str(n)] for d in range(10)})
    return list(rules.values())


RULES = rule_concepts()
N_RULES = len(RULES)
INTERVALS = [list(range(m, n + 1)) for m in NUMBERS for n in range(m, 101)]
MEMBERSHIP = np.array([np.isin(NUMBERS, c) for c in RULES + INTERVALS], dtype="float64")
CONCEPT_SIZE = MEMBERSHIP.sum(axis=1)
RULE_MEMBERSHIP = MEMBERSHIP[:N_RULES]
LOG_RULE_SIZE = np.log(CONCEPT_SIZE[:N_RULES])
# Centre so gamma does not trade off against lambda_0's normalisation.
LOG_RULE_SIZE_C = LOG_RULE_SIZE - LOG_RULE_SIZE.mean()


def set_log_lik(examples):
    """log P(examples | h) for every hypothesis, sampling distinct members without replacement."""
    total = np.zeros(len(MEMBERSHIP))
    shown = np.zeros(len(MEMBERSHIP))
    seen = set()
    for x in examples:
        if x in seen:  # a repeated number can only be a stray draw
            total += np.log((1 - ALPHA) / 100)
            continue
        seen.add(x)
        in_h = MEMBERSHIP[:, x - 1]
        remaining = np.maximum(CONCEPT_SIZE - shown, 1.0)
        total += np.log(ALPHA * in_h / remaining + (1 - ALPHA) / 100)
        shown += in_h
    return total


with pm.Model() as model:
    rule_log_lik = pm.Data("rule_log_lik", np.zeros((1, N_RULES)))  # (sets, rules): log P(D | r)
    interval_log_evidence = pm.Data("interval_log_evidence", np.zeros(1))  # (sets,)
    interval_in_concept = pm.Data("interval_in_concept", np.zeros((1, 100)))  # (sets, targets)
    row_cell = pm.Data("row_cell", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))  # set index * 100 + target - 1
    rating = pm.Data("rating", np.zeros(1, dtype="int64"))

    lambda_0 = pm.Beta("lambda_0", 2, 2)
    gamma = pm.Normal("gamma", 0.0, 1.0)  # prior preference for rule breadth
    log_rule_prior = gamma * LOG_RULE_SIZE_C
    log_rule_prior = log_rule_prior - pt.logsumexp(log_rule_prior)
    rule_joint = rule_log_lik + log_rule_prior[None, :]  # (sets, rules)
    rule_log_evidence = pt.logsumexp(rule_joint, axis=1)
    rule_post = pt.exp(rule_joint - rule_log_evidence[:, None])
    rule_in_concept = pt.dot(rule_post, RULE_MEMBERSHIP)  # (sets, targets)

    log_rules = pt.log(lambda_0) + rule_log_evidence
    log_intervals = pt.log1p(-lambda_0) - np.log(len(INTERVALS)) + interval_log_evidence
    p_rule = pm.math.sigmoid(log_rules - log_intervals)[:, None]
    in_concept = p_rule * rule_in_concept + (1 - p_rule) * interval_in_concept

    p_concept = pt.clip(in_concept.reshape((-1,))[row_cell], 0.0, 1.0)
    lapse = pm.Beta("lapse", 2, 8)
    guess_yes = pm.Beta("guess_yes", 2, 2)
    p_yes = pm.Deterministic("p_yes", pt.clip((1 - lapse) * p_concept + lapse * guess_yes, 1e-6, 1 - 1e-6))
    pm.Bernoulli("response", p=p_yes, observed=rating)


def prepare_observed(rows):
    """Rows carry `number_set` ("16,8", in presented order), `target` and `rating`."""
    sets = [tuple(int(x) for x in str(r["number_set"]).split(",")) for r in rows]
    unique = list(dict.fromkeys(sets))
    index = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(unique)}
    all_log_lik = np.stack([set_log_lik(s) for s in unique])
    interval_log_lik = all_log_lik[:, N_RULES:]
    interval_log_evidence = logsumexp(interval_log_lik, axis=1)
    return {
        "rule_log_lik": all_log_lik[:, :N_RULES],
        "interval_log_evidence": interval_log_evidence,
        "interval_in_concept": np.exp(interval_log_lik - interval_log_evidence[:, None]) @ MEMBERSHIP[N_RULES:],
        "row_cell": np.array([index[s] * 100 + int(r["target"]) - 1 for s, r in zip(sets, rows)], dtype="int64"),
        "rating": np.array([int(r["rating"]) for r in rows], dtype="int64"),
    }

I've written a refinement of the incumbent, `rule_breadth_prior_concepts`, called `concepts_sampled_without_replacement`. It passed the admission check with a smoke-fit log-likelihood of −904.3, against −904.8 for the incumbent. The gain is small, about half a nat, and its LOO score will most likely be statistically tied with the incumbent.

**The change:** People assume the program shows distinct numbers, so each new example is drawn from the concept's members that haven't been shown yet. The incumbent draws with replacement. This adds no parameters; everything else is kept: the 45 rules, all intervals, the size-graded rule prior, 10% random examples, and the guess lapse. The effect is strongest for small concepts the examples nearly use up. For example, after "8, 64" or "16, 8, 64" the learner is more sure the rule is "powers of 2", so it says "yes" less often to members of broader rules and wide ranges.

**How I chose it:** The critique found no significant discrepancies to target, so I tested other options against the incumbent's best fit of 903.3 (negative log-likelihood, lower is better):

| Variant | Extra parameters | Fit |
|---|---|---|
| Incumbent | – | 903.3 |
| Fuzzy edges on the number ranges | 1 | 903.2 |
| Breadth prior with a curved (quadratic) shape | 1 | 902.8 |
| Breadth preference scaled by the number of examples | 0 | 903.3 |
| Breadth preference divided by the number of examples | 0 | 904.0 |
| **Sampling without replacement** | **0** | **902.8** |

Without-replacement sampling matched the best fit without adding a parameter, so I went with it.
